question: Will the United States authorize the transfer of Tomahawk cruise missiles to Ukraine by October 30, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Ukraine has requested Tomahawks since Sept 2025; across ~13 months, including favorable windows (Pentagon green light Oct 2025, July 2026 thaw with Patriot co-production), no authorization occurred. As of Oct 15-19, 2026 the trend is sharply negative: Trump calls Zelensky 'not a good guy', has paused allied arms sales pending stockpile replenishment, waived the Russia sanctions act, and is publicly feuding with Kyiv; IISS-reported Tomahawk stocks depleted by the Iran war. ~11 days remain. Residual mass for a sudden leverage-driven reversal or an ambiguous statement read as authorization. Market: Polymarket's 2025-26 'Will Trump send Tomahawk to Ukraine' (~$605k vol) resolved NO for all dates; no current-window market found on Polymarket/Manifold; Kalshi/bookmakers not checked.
calls.dossier:
- Sept 2025: Ukraine formally requested Tomahawks; Oct 17, 2025 White House meeting: no yes (RFE/RL, NBC). Trump told Zelensky privately US would not provide them 'at least not yet' (The Hill).
- Oct 31, 2025: Pentagon gave White House 'green light' (stockpile not harmed); final decision left to Trump, who did not order transfer (CNN). Early Nov 2025: Trump said he was not considering supplying Tomahawks (Arms Control Assoc., Nov 2025).
- July 8-10, 2026: Trump shifted to praising Zelensky and approved Ukrainian production of Patriot missiles (Washington Post); Sept 2026 license reported (finchannel). No Tomahawk authorization in that thaw.
- Oct 15, 2026: CNN reports Ukraine ran out of Patriot interceptors amid Trump-Zelensky clash; Trump called Zelensky 'not a good guy' (military.com).
- Oct 15-16, 2026: Trump on Newsmax claimed US 'gave them massive amount of Patriots, Tomahawks' (Biden era); hromadske notes no confirmed Tomahawk transfer ever occurred. Trump said US halted allied ammunition sales until stockpiles replenished; Tomahawk production rising.
- Oct 16, 2026: Trump waived the Graham Russia sanctions act; Russia launched major strike on Ukraine energy grid that night (Silicon Curtain podcast commentary, partisan source; also claims Tomahawk promise was 'withdrawn').
- Oct 19, 2026: Trump defended easing pressure on Russia, blamed Zelensky for prolonging war; some Republicans criticized (Political Wire, citing WaPo).
- Oct 19, 2026: IISS (via newsroomamerica) says Iran war depleted Patriot/THAAD/Tomahawk stocks, replenishment 3+ years.
- Status quo: no authorization; resolves NO absent an official decision Oct 17-Oct 30.
- Base rate: 0 authorizations in ~13 monthly windows since Sept 2025 request, including two warmer periods (Oct 2025, Jul-Sep 2026).
- Resolution instrument: official presidential/DoD/White House decision to provide Tomahawks reported by credible media; 'considering' or Trump's retrospective claims that Tomahawks were given do not count.
- Event window: Oct 17, 2026 -> Oct 30, 2026 23:59 UTC; as of Oct 19 21:50 UTC ~22% elapsed.
- Markets: Polymarket 2025-26 Tomahawk market fully resolved; no current-window market found.
- Searched but not found: any report this week of a Tomahawk sale/transfer decision, any European purchase-for-Ukraine mechanism including Tomahawks.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: no authorization ever, hostile Oct 2026 context, depleted stocks, ~11 days left, no live market. The only open factual item is an unsourced search-summary claim (Run 2) of Oct 18, 2026 US-Ukraine technical talks on Tomahawk delivery. No run found a primary source; it conflicts with the Oct 15-19 reporting (arms sales paused, Trump hostile) and closely matches Oct 2025 news, so I treat it as likely conflation, at most a slight upward tilt. A partisan podcast's claim that a Tomahawk promise was 'withdrawn' is unverified and doesn't change the status quo either way. Remaining differences are judgment about tail size. I'd bet on ~1%, nudged slightly up for Trump's volatility and lenient-resolution risk.
